text.p: Foodland Associated Ltd maintains its prediction of stronger second half sales after reporting a slight decline in first half sales on Thursday, the company's managing director, Barry Alty said.

Asked in a telephone interview if Foodland was confident of an improvement in second half sales, Alty said: "Yes, we've held to the view and in fact predicted as far back as October that the first quarter, particularly in New Zealand, would be difficult because of the impact of the election."

Alty said the company's New Zealand operations were likely to benefit from increases in government spending and lower interest rates. A stronger performance from the company's Australian operations was not as easy to predict, he said.
"It's a bit up and down. There has been enough anecdotal evidence in newspapers of late that retail sales has been very difficult," he said.

"The pattern of the last several years has been quite unpredictable. You string a few really good months together and then fall back down a hole, there's no explanation for it - it's pretty difficult," Alty said.
Alty said he was hoping to see a further easing of interest rates in Australia. "I join the clamour," he said.
Foodland reported sales for the second quarter to January 26 fell 1.5 percent to A$977.95 million while sales for the 26 weeks to January 26 fell 0.9 percent to A$1.855 billion.

"Last year we lost a slice of our Western Australian wholesale business as a consequence of a cheque book marketing strategy from one of competitors and we are working at pegging that back," Alty said.
He said part of the strategy was the launch of independent banner groups in November and December.
"Although the impact of that doesn't fully reflect in the second quarter, we are very satisfied with the results and we think that will come through later on in the coming months."

Alty said a highlight of the second quarter performance was Action, the company's retail chain in Western Australia, which was undergoing a refurbishment program. "They have had very strong performance that's extremely pleasing," he said.
The other performance that was quite strong in relative terms was its New Zealand general merchandise group, Farmers Dekka, Alty said.
"It's been a very difficult trading environment in general merchandise in New Zealand as has been well demonstrated by the reported results of our peer companies over there," he said.
"Our performance, whilst flat is comparatively very strong."
At 1.10 p.m. (0210 GMT), Foodland shares were five cents weaker at A$6.01.
